title: Transport identifies the exchange map
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a finite discrete commutative ring. Let $\square=(f,f',g,g',\alpha)$ be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $f$ and $f'$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let $L\in\Dplus(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. On each pro-etale corner use precisely the constant ring $R_T=\Lambda_{T,\Proet}$ and its module category [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]; use the canonical structure isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map] on all four edges. Write $A_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism], $l_u=u_{\Et}^{-1}$, $r_u=Ru_{\Et,*}$, $p_u=Lu_{\Proet}^*$, $s_u=Ru_{\Proet,*}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $a_u:A_Ul_u\xrightarrow{\sim}p_uA_V$ be the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and let $b_u:A_Vr_u\xrightarrow{\sim}s_uA_U$ for $u=f,f'$ be the canonical counit-mate comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate], namely the transpose of $A_U\varepsilon_u^e\circ a_{u,r_u}^{-1}$. These are the specified direct-image comparison isomorphisms of [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image], with their normalization now made explicit.

Define
$$S_L=p_g(b_{f,L})\circ a_{g,r_fL}:A_{Y'}l_gr_fL\xrightarrow{\sim}p_gs_fA_XL,$$
$$T_L=s_{f'}(a_{g',L})\circ b_{f',l_{g'}L}:A_{Y'}r_{f'}l_{g'}L\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{f'}p_{g'}A_XL.$$
Let $E_L$ be the etale module exchange, the unit--square--counit mate of $\theta^e_\square:l_{f'}l_g\cong l_{g'}l_f$, using the module version of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] as identified by [lem-weil-pbc-module-abelian-derived-exchange-compatibility]. Then
$$T_L\circ A_{Y'}(E_L)=\Ex^{R}_{\square,A_XL}\circ S_L,$$
where $\Ex^R$ is precisely the ambient ringed unit--counit exchange of [def-weil-pbc-ambient-ringed-exchange]. Under the constant-ring identifications its source and target are $g_{\Proet}^{-1}Rf_{\Proet,*}A_XL$ and $Rf'_{\Proet,*}g'_{\Proet}{}^{-1}A_XL$, respectively. Thus conjugation by $S_L,T_L$ identifies the specified etale exchange with the specified pro-etale exchange.

proof.text: Check the ringed specialization first. For every edge $u$, put $c_u:u^{-1}R_V\cong R_U$ equal to the canonical constant-ring structure map. Both composites on the square take a constant scalar $\lambda$ to the same scalar; therefore the coefficient identifications agree under the chosen cartesian identification. The module pullback is $u^{-1}M\otimes_{u^{-1}R_V,c_u}R_U$. Its natural identification with the inverse image carrying the transported action is $m\otimes r\mapsto c_u^{-1}(r)m$, with inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$: the two composites are identities by tensor balancing. The operations node specifies this identification and the associated module adjunction. Exactness of this pullback implies that $p_u$ is computed termwise on any representing complex. For composable edges the two identifications send an iterated tensor $(m\otimes r)\otimes t$ to the same product of scalars acting on $m$; hence the composition isomorphism in the ringed square is precisely the inverse-image square isomorphism. We may consequently use the constant-module notation $p_u=u_{\Proet}^{-1}$, with its specified adjunction, throughout the following calculation.

source.place: Tags 03D2 (lemma-pullback-module), 03D3 (lemma-adjoint-push-pull-modules); explicit tensor identities in the identified-coefficient case

proof.text:
Fix all maps before calculating. The comparison $A_T$ is the finite-discrete-module comparison adjunction; the pullback comparisons are the specified $a_u$, not arbitrary natural isomorphisms. Apply the canonical-mate lemma to $f$ with input $L$ and to $f'$ with input $l_{g'}L$. The inverse-image functor $l_{g'}$ is exact, so it preserves bounded-below objects; thus the finite commutative coefficient, bounded-below, quasi-compact, and quasi-separated hypotheses are all met. This gives the invertible $b_f,b_{f'}$ together with the counit equations
$$\varepsilon^p_{u,A_UK}\circ p_u(b_{u,K})=A_U(\varepsilon^e_{u,K})\circ a_{u,r_uK}^{-1}\quad(u=f,f').$$
No normalization is inferred from the bare existence/coherence assertion of the older direct-image comparison node. On the etale side use the module unit--square--counit exchange. The module/abelian derived-exchange compatibility node identifies its fixed maps with the abelian exchange of the derived-exchange definition, so that this is a coefficient specialization rather than a change of exchange morphism.

source.place: Proof, specifying the two comparisons and the module exchange; normalization supplied by the new one-edge node

proof.text:
The corresponding unit face is forced by that counit equation. For $M\in D^+(V_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $u=f,f'$, set
$$h=s_u(a_{u,M})\circ b_{u,l_uM}\circ A_V(\eta^e_{u,M}):A_VM\to s_up_uA_VM.$$
Its transpose under $p_u\dashv s_u$ is, by naturality of the pro-etale counit followed by the displayed counit equation,
$$a_{u,M}\circ A_U(\varepsilon^e_{u,l_uM})\circ a_{u,r_ul_uM}^{-1}\circ p_uA_V(\eta^e_{u,M}).$$
Naturality of $a_u$ rewrites the last two factors as $A_Ul_u(\eta^e_{u,M})\circ a_{u,M}^{-1}$. The etale triangle identity makes this transpose $a_{u,M}\circ1\circ a_{u,M}^{-1}=1$. The unit $\eta^p_{u,A_VM}$ also has transpose $1$, so injectivity of the adjunction bijection gives $h=\eta^p_{u,A_VM}$. This proves the missing unit equation; invertibility of $b_u$ was not needed for this face.

proof.text:
Write $\theta^e:l_{f'}l_g\to l_{g'}l_f$ and $\theta^p:p_{f'}p_g\to p_{g'}p_f$ for the two specified square comparisons. Compatibility of $a_u$ with composites and the chosen cartesian identification says exactly
$$p_{g'}a_f\circ(a_{g'}l_f)\circ A_{X'}\theta^e=(\theta^p A_Y)\circ(p_{f'}a_g)\circ(a_{f'}l_g).$$
Both sides start at $A_{X'}l_{f'}l_g$ and end at $p_{g'}p_fA_Y$. This uses only the square-coherence clause of the pullback comparison statement, not any assertion about units or counits.

source.place: Proof, theta-square face, written as the explicit coherence equation

proof.text:
Compare the two arrows of the conclusion by taking their transposes under $p_{f'}\dashv s_{f'}$. Put $Z=A_{Y'}l_gr_fL$. Naturality of $\varepsilon^p_{f'}$, the $f'$ counit equation from step 2, and naturality of $a_{f'}$ give the transpose of $T_L\circ A_{Y'}E_L$ as
$$a_{g',L}\circ A_{X'}(\varepsilon^e_{f',l_{g'}L}\circ l_{f'}E_L)\circ a_{f',l_gr_fL}^{-1}.$$
By the defining etale mate formula, $\varepsilon^e_{f'}\circ l_{f'}E_L=l_{g'}(\varepsilon^e_{f,L})\circ\theta^e_{r_fL}$. Naturality of $a_{g'}$ and the step 4 square equation therefore turn this transpose into
$$p_{g'}\!\left(A_X\varepsilon^e_{f,L}\circ a_{f,r_fL}^{-1}\right)\circ\theta^p_{A_Yr_fL}\circ p_{f'}(a_{g,r_fL}).$$
The transpose of $\Ex^R_{\square,A_XL}\circ S_L$, using the defining ambient mate, is
$$p_{g'}\varepsilon^p_{f,A_XL}\circ\theta^p_{s_fA_XL}\circ p_{f'}p_g(b_{f,L})\circ p_{f'}(a_{g,r_fL}).$$
Move $b_{f,L}$ through $\theta^p$ by naturality to replace its first three factors by $p_{g'}(\varepsilon^p_f\circ p_f b_{f,L})\circ\theta^p_{A_Yr_fL}$. The $f$ counit equation of step 2 gives exactly the previous transpose. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves $T_L A_{Y'}E_L=\Ex^R S_L$. Since $S_L,T_L$ are isomorphisms, this is precisely the asserted conjugation identity. The cancellation rules used here are the mate-pasting calculus; their application has been exhibited at the level of these particular transposes.
